==English==
{{was wotd|2016|November|8}}
[[File:2014 Syrian presidential election day in Damascus (6).jpg|thumb|Women casting their votes during the {{w|2014 Syrian presidential election}}]]

===Etymology===
{{ety|en|:der|la:vōtum|tree=1}}
From {{der|en|la|vōtum}}, a form of {{m|la|voveō|t=to vow}} (cognate with {{cog|grc|εὔχομαι|t=to vow}}), from {{der|en|ine-pro|*h₁wegʷʰ-|t=to promise, to vow}}. {{doublet|en|vow}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/vəʊt/|a=RP}}
* {{IPA|en|/voʊt/|a=GA}}
** {{audio|en|en-us-vote.ogg|a=GA}}
* {{IPA|en|/vəʉt/|a=AU}}
* {{IPA|en|/(ʋ)oːʈ/|a=India}}
** {{hmp|en|oat|aa=dialectal,mainly <<South India>>}}
* {{rhymes|en|əʊt|s=1}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# A [[formalized]] [[choice]] on [[legally]] [[relevant]] [[measure]]s<!--rechtserhebliche Maßnahmen--> such as [[employment]] or [[appointment]] to [[office]] or a [[proceeding]] about a [[legal]] [[dispute]].
#: {{hypo|en|popular vote|electoral vote}}
#: {{ux|en|The city council decided the matter should go to public '''vote'''.}}
#: {{ux|en|Parliament will hold a '''vote''' of confidence regarding the minister.}}
#: {{ux|en|One occasion indicative '''votes''' were used was in 2003 when MPs were presented with seven different options on how to reform the House of Lords.}}
#* {{RQ:en:CNN|author=Matthew Robinson and Lianne Kolirin|title=The world has just redefined the kilogram|url=https://www.cnn.com/2018/11/13/world/kilo-measurement-scli-intl|date=2018-11-13|passage=Friday’s '''vote''' has permanently redefined the kilogram and sent Le Grand K into retirement.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260223063139/https://www.cnn.com/2018/11/13/world/kilo-measurement-scli-intl|archivedate=23 February 2026}}
# An act or instance of [[participate|participating]] in such a choice, e.g., by [[submit]]ting a [[ballot]].
#: {{ux|en|The Supreme Court upheld the principle of one person, one '''vote'''.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1862|origyear=1836|author=w:Oliver Wendell Holmes, Sr.|chapter=Poetry: A Metrical Essay|title=The Poems of Oliver Wendell Holmes|location=Boston, Mass.:|publisher=w:Ticknor and Fields|OCLC=5091562|pageurl=https://books.google.com/books?id=UF5AAAAAYAAJ&pg=PA8|pages=7–8|passage=There breathes no being but has some pretence / To that fine instinct called poetic sense; {{...}} / The freeman, casting with unpurchased hand / The '''vote''' that shakes the turrets of the land.}}
#* {{RQ:Birmingham Gossamer|I|01|As a political system democracy seems to me extraordinarily foolish, but I would not go out of my way to protest against it. My servant is, so far as I am concerned, welcome to as many '''votes''' as he can get. I would very gladly make mine over to him if I could.}}
#* [https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=celex%3A32017L0828 Directive (EU) 2017/828] amending {{w|Shareholder Rights Directive 2007|Directive 2007/36/EC}}, recital 10:
#*: {{quote|en|It is important to ensure that shareholders who engage with an investee company by voting know whether their '''votes''' have been correctly taken into account. Confirmation of receipt of '''votes''' should be provided in the case of electronic voting. In addition, each shareholder who casts a '''vote''' in a general meeting should at least have the possibility to verify after the general meeting whether the '''vote''' has been validly recorded and counted by the company.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2004|author=w:George Carlin|title=w:When Will Jesus Bring the Pork Chops?|url=https://archive.org/details/sacredmountainof0000john/|location=[[New York]]|publisher=w:Hyperion Books|ISBN=1-4013-0821-X|OCLC=757869006|OL=24604921M|page=158|pageurl=https://archive.org/details/whenwilljesusbri00hype/page/158/
|text=If you '''vote''' once, you're considered a good citizen. If you '''vote''' twice, you face four years in jail.}}
<!--# {{lb|en|metonymy}} somebody who counts with a vote, a [[voter]]. OED has such a sense but I tend to opine we shan’t include such metonymies. FF -->
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} An [[ardent]] [[wish#Noun|wish]] or [[desire#Noun|desire]]; a [[vow#Noun|vow]]; a [[prayer]].
#* '''1633''', {{w|Philip Massinger}}, “[[w:The Guardian (play)|The Guardian]]”, in ''Three New Playes; viz. The Bashful Lover, The Guardian, The Very Woman. As They have been Often Acted at the [[w:Blackfriars Theatre|Private-House in Black-Friers]], by [[w:King's Men (playing company)|His Late Majesties Servants]], with Great Applause'', London: Printed for {{w|Humphrey Moseley}}, and are to be sold at his Shop at the Sign of the Prince's Arms in [[w:St Paul's Cathedral|St. Pauls Church-yard]], published 1655, <small>{{w|OCLC}} [http://www.worldcat.org/oclc/15553475 15553475]</small>; republished as “The Guardian. A Comical History. As It hath been Often Acted at the Private-House in Black-Friars, by His Late Majesty's Servants, with Great Applause, 1655.”, in {{w|Thomas Coxeter}}, editor, ''The Works of Philip Massinger. Volume the Fourth. Containing, The Guardian. A Very Woman. The Old Law. The City Madam. And Poems on Several Occasions'', volume IV, London: Printed for [[w:Thomas Davies (bookseller)|T[homas] Davies]], in Russel-street, [[w:Covent Garden|Covent-Garden]], 1761, <small>{{w|OCLC}} [http://www.worldcat.org/oclc/6847259 6847259]</small>, Act V, scene i, [https://books.google.com/books?id=eTnuAAAAMAAJ&pg=PA71 page 71]:
#*: ''Jol''[''ante'']. In you, Sir, / I live; and when, or by the Courſe of Nature, / Or Violence you muſt fall, the End of my / Devotions is, that one and the ſame Hour / May make us fit for Heaven. // ''Server''. I join with you / In my '''votes''' that way: {{...}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} A formalized [[petition]] or [[request]].
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} Any [[judgment]] of [[intellect]] leading to a [[formal]] [[opinion]], a [[point of view]].
# Any [[judgment]] of [[intellect]] leading not only to a [[formal]] [[opinion]] but also to a particular [[choice]] in a legally relevant measure, a [[point of view]] as published.
#: {{ux|en|dissenting '''vote''' (i.e. in particular the differing opinion published with a judicial judgment considered as a source of information)}}
# {{lb|en|NZ}} a spending area or group of [[appropriation]]s within the national budget, representing specific sectors, departments or functional areas.
#*: {{quote|en|'''Votes''' are an appropriation or groupings of appropriations. Appropriations are parliamentary authorisation for the Crown or an Office of Parliament to incur expenses or capital expenditure that are administered by Ministers of the Crown or the Speaker of the House of Representatives.}}

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[cast#Verb|cast]] a vote; to assert a formalized choice in an [[election]].
#: {{ux|en|Q: Did you '''vote''' last month? A: Yes. I '''voted''' for John Smith, and it's a shame that he lost; you can't blame me for the mess we're in now.}}
#: {{ux|en|The directors '''voted''' on the question of whether to increase the R&D spending.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=2020-09-24|author=Keshava Guha|title=Letters|journal=w:London Review of Books|volume=42|issue=18|url=https://www.lrb.co.uk/the-paper/v42/n17/christian-lorentzen/i-need-money|passage=The Violence against Women Act was not distinct from the Crime Bill but an integral part of it. {{...}} Sanders has subsequently cited the inclusion of the VAWA as his reason for '''voting''' for the overall bill, on the rather Bidenian principle that the perfect should not be the enemy of the good.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260907193845/https://www.lrb.co.uk/the-paper/v42/n17/christian-lorentzen/i-need-money|archivedate=7 September 2026}}
#* {{RQ:en:CNN|author=Aaron Blake|title=Americans voted for deportations. They didn’t necessarily vote for this.|url=https://www.cnn.com/2025/06/11/politics/deportations-trump-polling-analysis|date=2025-06-11|passage=Americans '''voted''' for deportations when a plurality backed Donald Trump – who’d spoken openly about his plans on the trail – last November. But they didn’t necessarily '''vote''' for this.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260812204952/https://www.cnn.com/2025/06/11/politics/deportations-trump-polling-analysis|archivedate=12 August 2026}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[choose]] or [[grant]] (some objective) by means of a vote, or by general consent.
#: {{ux|en|The directors '''voted''' an increase in R&D spending.}}
#: {{ux|en|The meal was '''voted''' a great success.
}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To exercise one's voting right upon (a ballot or a share of stock).
#: {{coi|en|'''vote''' your ballot}};   {{coi|en|'''vote''' your shares}}
#: {{ux|en|Please '''vote''' your ballot using black or blue ink, then seal your ballot inside the privacy envelope.}}
#: {{ux|en|The depository may '''vote''' shares on behalf of investors who have not submitted instruction to the bank.}}
